items.title: Connecticut judge says CFTC cannot override court's reading of federal law in Kalshi case
items.content_text: - **Connecticut judge says CFTC cannot override court's reading of federal law in Kalshi case** — U.S. District Judge Vernon D. Oliver ruled the CFTC cannot override his court's reading of federal law in Kalshi's Connecticut case, finding the agency's August market emergency order does not change his earlier conclusion that Kalshi's sports-event contracts are not swaps under the Commodity Exchange Act. The CFTC issued the order after New York Attorney General Letitia James sued Kalshi in state court; Connecticut's gaming laws stand. ([GambleRss](https://gamblerss.com/connecticut-judge-says-cftc-cannot-override-court-s-reading-of-federal-law-in-prediction-markets-case-67760))

items.title: Kalshi seeks full 6th Circuit review of states' regulation win
items.content_text: - **Kalshi seeks full 6th Circuit review of states' regulation win** — Kalshi asked the full Sixth Circuit to review a three-judge panel ruling that Ohio and Tennessee can regulate it as unlicensed online sports gambling, arguing the panel erred and pointing to the CFTC's same-day proposals defining sports and other event contracts as federal swaps. The en banc petition, filed October 9, extends the industry's latest legal fight over whether state gambling laws reach federally registered prediction markets. items.title: 39 states, NFL, Dodd and Gensler file Supreme Court amicus briefs as CFTC moves to classify prediction contracts as swaps
items.content_text: - **39 states, NFL, Dodd and Gensler file Supreme Court amicus briefs as CFTC moves to classify prediction contracts as swaps** — Last week 39 states plus D.C., 145 tribal nations, the NFL, former Senator Chris Dodd and former CFTC chair Gary Gensler filed amicus briefs urging the Supreme Court to take up whether sports prediction contracts qualify as swaps, with most siding with state authority. On Friday the CFTC answered with an interim final rule and a new proposal explicitly classifying sports, political and other event contracts as federal swaps; Kalshi's deadline to respond was extended to November 9. ([KuCoin](https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/39-states-and-cftc-clash-over-regulation-of-sports-prediction-markets))

items.title: NFL files amicus brief backing Supreme Court review of CFTC authority over prediction markets
items.content_text: - **NFL files amicus brief backing Supreme Court review of CFTC authority over prediction markets** — The NFL filed an amicus brief backing New Jersey's cert petition against Kalshi, asking the Supreme Court to clarify whether the CFTC has exclusive jurisdiction over sports event contracts. The league cites consumer harm, game-integrity risks and underage betting, while critics note the NFL has a financial interest in keeping prediction markets regulated like traditional sportsbooks. items.content_text: - **CFTC sues Wisconsin in fifth state lawsuit asserting jurisdiction over prediction markets** — The CFTC sued Wisconsin in federal court in the agency's fifth lawsuit against a US state over prediction-market jurisdiction, responding to the state's suits against Kalshi, Polymarket, Crypto.com, Robinhood and Coinbase. items.title: Wisconsin judge rejects CFTC injunction bid against state prediction-market crackdown
items.content_text: - **Wisconsin judge rejects CFTC injunction bid against state prediction-market crackdown** — U.S. District Judge William C. Griesbach denied the CFTC's bid to block Wisconsin's enforcement against prediction-market platforms, ruling the agency showed neither irreparable harm nor a likelihood of success on the merits. The setback lands days after a Minnesota federal judge granted a preliminary injunction stopping a state ban, deepening the circuit split the Supreme Court is being asked to resolve. ([SBC Americas](https://sbcamericas.com/2026/07/29/wisconsin-judge-denies-cftc-injunction/))

items.content_text: - **Kalshi and Polymarket midterm markets face insider-trading scrutiny over knowable contracts** — A new Anti-Corruption Data Collective analysis, first reported by CNN, flags the platforms' hyper-specific midterm election contracts as vulnerable to political insider trading, with more than $20 million in volume on so-called knowable markets.
